item.text: {"text":"No exact SASRec-plus-gated-recent-mean method with the complete requested ablation suite was verified. Closest precedent: [HGN (KDD 2019)](https://arxiv.org/html/1906.09217), which applies feature and instance gates to recent item embeddings before average pooling, then combines this representation with user preferences and item–item products. SASRec is a comparator, not its backbone. Ablations cover gate removal, average versus max pooling, and GRU/CNN alternatives; parameter counts are reported, but those alternatives are not parameter-matched. [HAM](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10034966/) supplies an important ungated precedent: mean pooling over short and longer recent windows, with interaction-trained embeddings and comparisons against HGN/SASRec. Neither establishes the exact proposed residual design or its novelty.\n\nThe [original SASRec implementation](https://github.com/kang205/SASRec/blob/master/model.py) specifies causal attention, zero-padded item embeddings, masking after embedding dropout and each block, normalization before attention queries and feed-forward layers, and final normalization before scoring. It contains no recent-mean fusion gate. The inspected HGN paper does not specify padding treatment or gate initialization sufficiently to reproduce those details. A reproducible experimental proposal—not a verified published recipe—is m_t=Σ mask_j E[x_j]/max(1,Σ mask_j) over j∈[max(1,t−k+1),t], followed by z_t=h_t+sigmoid(a)m_t, initializing a=−3 and learning ID embeddings from scratch. Compare SASRec alone, last-item residual, fixed-weight recent-mean residual, learned scalar gate, and a parameter-matched branch using h_t alone; separately vary normalization before/after fusion. Keep pooling causal at every training position and normalization identical across information-source ablations."}
